summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes 727KB obfuscated sibling payload on npm install
details: @onereach/ssml-editor advertises itself as a Vue SSML editor component but declares an npm preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, on every `npm install`, downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime archive from oven-sh/bun GitHub releases (v1.3.13), extracts it, chmods it executable, and then invokes that freshly-downloaded Bun binary via execFileSync to run a bundled 727KB file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a Bun-compiled bundle (// @bun @bun-cjs header) with string-array rotation obfuscation (a `WV8StW` shift routine and a large `n7gIxM` numeric constant table) and a minified single-line body; it is not referenced by the package's stated Vue entry (src/App.vue) and is only reachable through setup.mjs and the downloaded Bun runtime. A Vue UI component has no legitimate need to fetch a second JavaScript runtime and use it to execute an opaque obfuscated blob at install time. The combination — install-time fetch of an alternate runtime + execution of a shipped, purpose-mismatched, heavily-obfuscated payload under that runtime — grants arbitrary code execution on any developer or CI machine that installs this version.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
